gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's US price per cell. Here they are: Panasonic eneloop $3.12 a cell ($24.99 for 8 at District Camera). IKEA LADDA 2450 and Tenergy Premium Pro 2800 are both $3.00 a cell in a $11.99 4-pack, and Tenergy drops to $2.15 a cell in its $42.99 20-pack. Panasonic eneloop pro is $4.99 a cell even in its cheapest pack (8 for $39.95) and $6.23 in the 4-pack ($24.90 at District Camera). Divided by the makers' rated cycles, a standard eneloop costs about $0.0015 per charge and an eneloop pro about $0.010, roughly 7× more.
standout_why: Digital Camera World (cited, updated 2026-05-18) names eneloop pro, eneloop, EBL 2800, HiQuick 2800, the EBL 1.5 V Li-ion and Energizer Recharge Power Plus, but the readable part of the page shows no prices and no cost per cell or per cycle. The Which? sample page (cited, 2026-04-27) prices only in pounds (£9.80 average for LADDA, £15.15 for Energizer Recharge Extreme) and doesn't cover eneloop or Tenergy at all. ChatGPT's own answer gives pack prices with different pack sizes (eneloop $24.99 for 8, eneloop pro $13.75 for 4, LADDA $11.99 for 4) and never works out a per-cell or per-cycle cost. It also never mentions Tenergy Premium Pro, which costs the same as LADDA for a 4-pack. I couldn't confirm the $13.75 eneloop pro price: I didn't find The Camerashop's listing, and District Camera charges $24.90 for the same 4-pack today.
decides: It backs eneloop as the pick for most people. Per cell it costs about the same as LADDA ($3.12 vs $3.00), and Panasonic's 2,100-cycle rating against Which?'s finding that LADDA keeps only about two-thirds of its capacity after 200 cycles makes eneloop the cheapest per charge. Eneloop pro should be sold only for flashes and high-drain gear: per cell it costs at least 60% more than standard eneloop, and it is rated for about a quarter of the cycles. In the 'best value' slot, Tenergy Premium Pro matches LADDA's $11.99 price and is rated higher (2,800 vs 2,450 mAh, 1,200 cycles, 85% kept after a year), you can order it online rather than going to an IKEA, and it is ours. But those are only Tenergy's ratings, with no independent test, so they should be presented as maker figures. The XTAR 1.5 V lithium costs about $7 a cell and only makes sense for devices that misread 1.2 V NiMH.
